neighbours.label: Prepositions and determiners in planetary-scale geography, where the next word is space, an ocean or the planet (from outer space, stretches of the Pacific, reaching the Earth), vs the same frames at local scale (rivers, rooms, gardens)
fire: The astronaut took a photo of the reef from outer space.
Most of the heat radiates back into space at night.
The storm travelled across thousands of miles of the Pacific Ocean.
Very little of the solar energy reaching the Earth is absorbed by the poles.
The probe was launched into deep space in 1977.
Cold currents flow along the floor of the Indian Ocean.
Debris from old satellites falls back to the planet every week.
The whales migrate across the open waters of the Southern Ocean.
quiet: The tourist took a photo of the bridge from the hotel window.
Most of the heat escapes through the kitchen window at night.
The boat travelled down several miles of the Thames.
Very little of the rain reaching the garden soaks into the clay.
The ball was kicked into the next yard in 1977.
Cold water flows along the bottom of the village stream.
Leaves from the old oak fall onto the lawn every week.
The ducks paddle across the still waters of the town pond.

predictions: The preposition/'outer'/'the' before space/ocean/planet reaches 0.4-0.85; the same frames with a river, room or town stay under 0.1.
short: slot before space/ocean/planet at planetary scale
notes: Card: top 32 peak on ' the', ' outer', ' of', ' into' before space/ocean/Earth/planet; the + pole promotes river words and suppresses space/oceans. Probe: from outer space 0.836, stretches of the Atlantic 0.545, into space 0.446, planet's 0.433; stretches of the Mississippi 0.049, children from the garden 0.009. 'into the room' in a greenhouse-heat sentence also fired 0.446, so the earlier context sets it: near misses change the whole scene.
